findings.title: Unhandled ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT Server Exception in SSE Endpoint When Connection Limit Is Exceeded
findings.evidence: events() in publicController.js sets res.status(200), flushes headers, and writes ': connected\n\n' BEFORE invoking addRealtimeClient(res). When clients.size >= MAX_SSE_CLIENTS (100), addRealtimeClient attempts res.status(429).json({ success: false, message: 'Too many connections' }), triggering an unhandled 'Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client'.
findings.scenario: Under normal web traffic when 100 clients are connected to SSE, user 101 connecting triggers an uncaught ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT exception. Client reconnection loops exacerbate the issue, repeatedly throwing unhandled exceptions in the Node HTTP server pipeline.
findings.impact: Server instability, error logging spikes, Sentry alert flooding, broken client connection state, and complete failure to communicate rate limiting to overflowing clients.
findings.reproduction: Simulate 100 concurrent SSE connections to /api/public/events. On the 101st request, observe the Node.js server throw ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT when attempting to set status 429.
findings.remediation: Check capacity (clients.size >= MAX_SSE_CLIENTS) in events() BEFORE setting HTTP 200 headers. If at capacity, immediately return res.status(429).json(...) before stream headers are written. In routes/public.js, wrap events in asyncHandler, and in middleware/error.js ensure res.headersSent is checked before attempting error serialization.
findings.regressionTest: Mock clients.size = 100 and issue a GET request to /api/public/events. Assert response status is 429 and no ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT exception is thrown.

findings.title: Complete Denial of Realtime Updates via Global Rate Limit Bypass and Uncapped Per-IP SSE Connections
findings.evidence: In backend/src/app.js, express-rate-limit explicitly skips /api/public/events via skip: (req) => ... req.path === '/api/public/events'. There is no per-IP connection limit, no IP-based rate limiting on /api/public/events, and no authentication required.
findings.scenario: An unauthenticated remote attacker or misconfigured client opens 100 parallel EventSource connections from a single IP. All 100 connections are accepted and occupy every slot up to MAX_SSE_CLIENTS = 100.
findings.impact: Total denial of service for the realtime update subsystem. Every other user across the entire platform is blocked from receiving live CMS updates, and any new visitor triggers the ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT exception.
findings.reproduction: Script 100 concurrent GET requests from a single client IP to /api/public/events. All 100 are accepted without rate limiting, holding all server SSE slots.
findings.remediation: Implement per-IP connection limits (e.g., maximum 3-5 concurrent SSE connections per client IP) and apply a dedicated rate limiter (e.g., max 10 connection attempts per 5 minutes) on /api/public/events.
findings.regressionTest: Attempt 6 concurrent SSE connections from a single IP address. Assert that connections exceeding the per-IP threshold are rejected with HTTP 429.

findings.title: Socket and File Descriptor Leak Due to Missing res.end() on SSE Lifetime Expiration
findings.evidence: In realtime.js, const cleanup = () => { clearInterval(heartbeat); clearTimeout(lifetime); clients.delete(res); }. When the 1-hour MAX_SSE_LIFETIME_MS timeout triggers, cleanup() removes the client from clients and clears timers, but never calls res.end() or destroys the socket.
findings.scenario: When long-running clients remain connected past 1 hour, heartbeats cease, but the underlying TCP connection and Node response stream remain open indefinitely in memory.
findings.impact: Gradual socket, memory, and file descriptor leakage on the server, eventually degrading OS network resources.
findings.reproduction: Temporarily set MAX_SSE_LIFETIME_MS to 1000ms. Open an SSE connection. After 1s, verify client is removed from clients set, but the TCP socket remains in ESTABLISHED state without FIN packet being sent.
findings.remediation: In cleanup(), explicitly call if (!res.writableEnded) { res.end(); } to terminate the HTTP response stream when lifetime expires.
findings.regressionTest: Trigger the lifetime expiration timer and assert that res.writableEnded becomes true and socket terminates.

findings.title: Unrestricted Public Exposure and Gated Bypass of Draft, Internal, and Bespoke Enterprise Plans
findings.evidence: Plan.js schema defines only active: { type: Boolean, default: true } without isPublic, published, or isDraft. CatalogService.getActivePlans() queries Plan.find({ active: true }). PaymentService.createOrder allows purchase of any Plan.findOne({ _id: planId, active: true }).
findings.scenario: An admin creates a custom corporate plan, draft pricing experiment, or internal test tier. Because it defaults to active: true, it immediately appears in the public /api/catalog/plans feed and becomes purchasable by any authenticated user via /api/payments/order.
findings.impact: Business and pricing logic leakage, unintended public purchase of internal or negotiated enterprise contracts, and inability to stage plans in draft mode.
findings.reproduction: Insert a plan with custom negotiated rates for a specific client. Query GET /api/catalog/plans; verify the custom negotiated plan is returned in the public catalog.
findings.remediation: Add isPublic: { type: Boolean, default: true } and isDraft: { type: Boolean, default: false } to Plan.js. Filter by { active: true, isPublic: true, isDraft: false } in CatalogService.getActivePlans(), and validate entitlement eligibility in PaymentService.
findings.regressionTest: Create a plan with active: true, isPublic: false. Query GET /api/catalog/plans and assert the plan is omitted.

findings.title: High-Concurrency Database Bottleneck: Missing Compound Indexes on All CMS Collections (COLLSCAN)
findings.evidence: Queries executed on public routes: Service.find({ active: true }).sort({ category: 1, price: 1 }), Plan.find({ active: true }).sort({ category: 1, price: 1 }), FAQ.find({ active: true }).sort({ order: 1, createdAt: 1 }), Partner.find({ active: true }).sort({ order: 1, createdAt: 1 }). None of these collections define compound indexes matching their filter and sort keys. ensure-indexes.js omitted CMS collections entirely.
findings.scenario: High-traffic bursts on the public homepage or pricing page cause simultaneous unindexed collection scans and memory sort operations across all CMS collections.
findings.impact: Elevated MongoDB CPU usage, slow response times, and degraded throughput under public traffic spikes.
findings.reproduction: Run explain('executionStats') on Service.find({ active: true }).sort({ category: 1, price: 1 }). Verify executionStages.stage is COLLSCAN followed by in-memory SORT.
findings.remediation: Add schema indexes: Service.index({ active: 1, category: 1, price: 1 }), Plan.index({ active: 1, category: 1, price: 1 }), FAQ.index({ active: 1, order: 1, createdAt: 1 }), Partner.index({ active: 1, order: 1, createdAt: 1 }). Update ensure-indexes.js.
findings.regressionTest: Execute explain('executionStats') and assert query plan utilizes IXSCAN with 0 documents examined outside the index.

findings.title: Internal MongoDB ObjectIds and Administrative Activity Broadcast to Anonymous Public SSE Listeners
findings.evidence: broadcastCmsUpdate broadcasts key: String(item._id) along with resource and action ('created', 'updated', 'deleted') to all connected public /api/public/events clients. This occurs even when draft resources or unpublished pages are created or modified.
findings.scenario: An anonymous observer maintains an open EventSource connection to /api/public/events and records real-time notifications revealing internal database ObjectIds, admin creation timing, and unpublished resource identifiers.
findings.impact: Reconnaissance information disclosure; leaks database internal identifiers and operational patterns to unauthenticated users.
findings.reproduction: Listen to /api/public/events with curl. Create a page in admin. Observe the received SSE payload contains the raw MongoDB ObjectId.
findings.remediation: Sanitize the broadcast payload to emit only resource category invalidation signals (e.g. { resource: 'plans', action: 'updated', timestamp: '...' }) without leaking internal MongoDB ObjectIds.
findings.regressionTest: Trigger broadcastCmsUpdate({ resource: 'pages', key: '507f1f77bcf86cd799439011' }). Assert message payload does not expose raw database IDs to public consumers.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Cache-Control and In-Memory/Redis Caching on Public CMS and Catalog Endpoints
findings.evidence: Compare bookController.js:13 (Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600...) with catalogController.js and publicController.js: zero caching headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified) are sent on /api/catalog/services, /api/catalog/plans, /api/public/faqs, /api/public/partners, /api/public/settings/:key, or /api/public/pages/:slug. Furthermore, no in-memory or Redis caching layer is implemented despite having Redis and realtime event invalidations.
findings.scenario: Every request from every client or CDN edge results in a fresh database query for static content that rarely changes.
findings.impact: Unnecessary database load and higher TTFB for landing page visitors.
findings.reproduction: Request GET /api/catalog/plans. Check response headers; observe absence of Cache-Control and ETag.
findings.remediation: Add Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600 on public catalog and CMS endpoints, or cache serialized results in Redis invalidated via broadcastCmsUpdate.
findings.regressionTest: Send GET request to /api/catalog/plans. Assert Cache-Control header is present with public cache directives.

findings.title: Missing Input Validation Schemas and Unbounded Queries on Public CMS Route Parameters
findings.evidence: There are no validator files (catalog.validator.js and public.validator.js do not exist). req.params.slug in /api/public/pages/:slug has no format or length validation, and queries in catalog.service.js and public.service.js lack .limit() or pagination.
findings.scenario: Oversized or malformed parameters are passed directly to database queries, and unbounded queries return all records without limit.
findings.impact: Input validation gap; potential query resource consumption if collections grow large.
findings.reproduction: Send GET request to /api/public/pages/ with an oversized 10,000-character parameter string. Request reaches MongoDB query directly without route rejection.
findings.remediation: Implement Zod validator middleware for public routes validating slug format ^[a-z0-9-]+$ (max 100 characters) and add reasonable default limits (e.g. .limit(100)) on collection queries.
findings.regressionTest: Send GET request to /api/public/pages/invalid*slug!. Assert request is rejected with 400 ZOD_VALIDATION_ERROR.
